question.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+6x+4y=19?$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+6x+4y & =19 \\ 3{x}^{2}+6x-{y}^{2}+4y & =19 \\ 3[{x}^{2}+2x]-[{y}^{2}-4y] & =19 \\ 3[(x+1)^{2}-1]-[(y-2)^{2}-4] & =19 \\ 3(x+1)^{2}-3-(y-2)^{2}+4 & =19 \\ 3(x+1)^{2}-(y-2)^{2} & =19+3-4 \\ 3(x+1)^{2}-(y-2)^{2} & =18 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{6}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{18} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(-1,2).$
